title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point treats sunlight and wind as continuous, which conflicts with the brief's renewable classification, and the other is a Year 11 Geography card at a different depth, so neither fits this Year 7-8 Science point without substantial rewriting.

draft.title: Renewable and non-renewable resources
card: A resource is something from Earth that people use, such as water, soil, wind or coal.
a resource that nature can replace within a human lifetime. Sunlight, wind and timber from managed forests are examples.
a resource that is used much faster than nature can make it, so it cannot be replaced in a human lifetime. Coal, oil and metal ores are examples.
Coal and oil formed from living things over millions of years. A renewable resource can still run short if it is used faster than it is replaced.
draft.remember: Renewable: replaced in a human lifetime. Non-renewable: not.

a.q: Which of these is a non-renewable resource?
opts: Iron ore dug from a mine
a.why: Iron ore took a very long time to form in the ground, so it cannot be replaced in a human lifetime. Timber from a managed forest is tempting, but new trees can be grown within a lifetime.
a.clue: Which one could not be replaced in your lifetime?

b.q: A town in Gippsland burns oil for power. Another town plants new trees for timber each time it cuts some down. Which statement is correct?
opts: Oil is non-renewable, and the planted timber is renewable
Oil is renewable, because it is found in many places
Timber is non-renewable, because trees take years to grow
Both are non-renewable, because both are used up
b.why: Oil formed over millions of years, so it cannot be replaced in a human lifetime. Trees can be regrown within a lifetime, so timber is renewable even though growth takes years.
b.clue: Compare the time to replace each one with a human lifetime.

a.best: Iron ore dug from a mine

b.best: Oil is non-renewable, and the planted timber is renewable
